subject: Observability mosaic: pricing structure & tradeoffs for retention, tracing, dashboards
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Zhao <elliot.zhao@cloudmosaic.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability mosaic: pricing structure & tradeoffs for retention, tracing, dashboards

Elliot —

Great to meet you on the call earlier. Per our conversation, CloudMosaic is evaluating a single vendor for model inference + ops visibility and asked us to scope the add-on pricing for:
- long-term log/trace retention (30/90/365 day buckets)
- full-trace vs sampled tracing costs
- advanced dashboards (custom visual widgets, replays, saved queries)

Attached are two artifacts to start: a short SOW draft (high level scope) and a simple retention cost model (workbook) showing slab vs metered scenarios. A few quick framing notes so we can align on the right packaging: 

1) Slab (flat retention buckets): predictable, easier to budget at scale; better for customers who keep long-tail access.
2) Metered (ingest/retention metering): lower up-front commitment, more elastic, can be more expensive if retention grows unexpectedly.
3) Tracing: we price full-trace ingestion separately; customers can choose head-sampling (80/20) or tail-retain for small subsets to reduce cost.

Proposed shortlist of commercial options (high level):
A) Pilot: 3-month pilot, 30-day retention slab, pilot credits $6k, no surcharge for dashboards.
B) 12-month commit: 15% discount on add-ons, 90-day retention slab included, 1 onboarding credit (waived setup fee).
C) Enterprise: custom term (365-day bucket), volume discount (20%+), dedicated support + can carve seats for dashboard concurrency.

Can you confirm CloudMosaic's current 99th percentile trace volume (avg spans/s) and whether you need full raw-trace replay for compliance? That will drive the delta between slab and metered.

Next steps: if you’re comfortable, we’ll convert the SOW to a pricing quote and route to procurement. I’ve also built a quick worksheet that shows cost at 30/90/365 days across three traffic growth scenarios — see retention_cost_model.xlsx.

Available windows this week for a short follow-up: Tue/Thu 10–11am PT, Wed 2–4pm PT.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: CloudMosaic_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (PDF stub)
Attachment: retention_cost_model.xlsx (Excel stub)
From: Elliot Zhao <elliot.zhao@cloudmosaic.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@cloudmosaic.com
Date: 2026-06-02T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability mosaic: pricing structure & tradeoffs for retention, tracing, dashboards

Ben —

Thanks for the materials and the clear options. A few follow-ups from our side (inline):

> Can you confirm CloudMosaic's current 99th percentile trace volume (avg spans/s)?

We currently average ~1,200 spans/s at peak traffic, with bursts to ~4k for short windows (CI traffic, deployment spikes).

> Do you need full raw-trace replay for compliance?

We have two teams: Platform (needs raw replays for debugging) and Security/Compliance (needs sampled full-fidelity for incident investigations). For now, we’d like the option to retain full-trace for 30 days and sampled tails for 365 days.

We also have procurement questions:
- Can you provide a simple one-pager that maps the slab vs metered cost at our volumes (30/90/365) so our finance team can model the delta?
- For the 12-month commit, is the 15% discount applied only to add-ons, or to the entire package (inference + add-ons)?
- What’s your recommended delta for trace sampling to give us the best cost-quality tradeoff?

We’d like a short demo of the advanced dashboards — Wed 3pm PT works. I’ll invite the Platform lead and procurement.

Thanks,
Elliot Zhao
CloudMosaic — Head of Platform

On Tue, Jun 1, 2026 at 9:12 AM Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elliot —
> 
> Great to meet you on the call earlier. Per our conversation, CloudMosaic is evaluating...
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Zhao <elliot.zhao@cloudmosaic.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, procure@cloudmosaic.com
Date: 2026-06-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability mosaic: pricing structure & tradeoffs for retention, tracing, dashboards

Elliot — thanks for the details, that helps a lot. Quick answers and a pragmatic recommendation inline.

1) At 1.2k spans/s sustained (4k peaks): the retention_cost_model.xlsx shows approximate monthly delta:
- 30-day slab: $6.5k/mo
- 90-day slab: $14k/mo
- 365-day slab: $45k/mo
Metered (ingest+store): about 10–18% higher at current volumes assuming no aggressive sampling.

2) Sampling recommendation: start with 80/20 head-sample (capture top 80% of traces fully, tail-sample 20% for anomalies) — that often captures 90% of debugging value while cutting trace cost ~40%. We can tune per-service.

3) Discount question: the 15% on a 12-month commit applies to add-ons only in our standard offer; we can consider extending to the full bundle under a packaged ARR threshold (we've done this for a small set of reference accounts). If you’re targeting a consolidated ARR commit, I can model two scenarios (add-ons only vs full-bundle).

4) Demo: Wed 15:00 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite and a pre-demo checklist.

Commercial proposal — two options I’d recommend for CloudMosaic given your profile: 
Pilot path (low risk): 3 months, 30d retention slab, $6k credit, dashboards included.
Commit path (predictable ops): 12-month commit for add-ons with 15% off add-ons, includes 90d slab. We’ll offer a one-time onboarding credit of $10k to offset integration work.

If procurement wants a single-page slab vs metered comparison at your volume points I’ll produce that doc this afternoon and upload to the Drive link. In the meantime I’m attaching an edited cost model with the sampling scenario baked in.

Next steps:
- Ben to produce 1-pager and upload to shared Drive (today) — Ben
- Schedule demo (Wed 3pm PT) — Ben/Elliot
- Procurement to confirm preferred commercial path for internal modeling — CloudMosaic

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention_cost_model_sampled_scenarios.xlsx (Excel stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-03T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: CloudMosaic concession ask — onboarding credit approval

Quick internal note — CloudMosaic is leaning to the 12-month add-on commit but procurement asked for a $10k onboarding credit and dashboard concurrency waiver for the pilot. I proposed the $10k onboarding credit (one-time) and to keep dashboard concurrency in the standard seat model.

Can you approve the one-time $10k credit and an exception to waive the setup fee? If we want to push for the full-bundle discount (extend 15% to inference), we should ask for a minimum ARR commit of $550k to justify.

Why it’s OK: CloudMosaic is a solid reference candidate, high visibility in our target vertical, and they show an appetite for scaling to enterprise terms in year two.

If no objections I’ll accept the concession and close the pilot terms, then route a formal quote to procurement.

—Ben

Approve the $10k onboarding credit and waive the setup fee for the pilot. We should reserve the right to revisit dashboard concurrency pricing on renewal. If they ask to extend the 15% to inference, push for the $550k ARR or else we stick to add-ons-only discount.
